summary: Dry-style beet curry with mustard oil, black mustard and cumin seeds, onion, garlic, ginger, turmeric and tamarind: 3 pounds of cubed red beets (and their greens) simmered covered 20-30 minutes until very tender, finished with garam masala; serves 4.
glance: 20-30 minutes, covered, until the beets are very tender
3 pounds red beets (about 3 medium bunches), peeled and cubed
basmati rice, raita and chana mushroom masala
faq: Why mustard oil and mustard seed with beets?
Those flavors go so well with beets. If you don't have mustard oil, use all vegetable oil and maybe add more seeds. Use black mustard seeds, not the light brown or yellow ones.
Why add tamarind?
A bit of tamarind concentrate dissolved in hot water provides acid balance against the sweet earthiness of the beets. The author uses Tamicon brand; you may need more if yours is less concentrated.
Can I use the beet greens?
Yes. Rinse, roughly chop and add them on top of the beets for extra nutrition and flavor. They make the curry look slightly less lovely, but the author hates to waste a good ingredient.
Does the curry have a sauce?
No, it's a dry style curry, though the beets are moist. Remove the lid and simmer off any remaining water, adding more water during the cook if needed.
Where did the author first eat beet curry?
Over a campfire in Hot Springs, Arkansas, cooked by a girlfriend who had lived in Tamil Nadu for a year.

summary: Creamy grits with crispy leeks, a morita and honey leek jus and cilantro-epazote pesto: stone-ground grits simmered about 45 minutes in water and milk, topped with a fried or poached egg, queso fresco and the fried leeks; a Southwestern take on breakfast for dinner for 2.
glance: 1 cup stone-ground in 3 cups water and 1 cup milk, simmered about 45 minutes
3, fried in 1/4 cup oil until deep brown; the rest simmered with moritas and honey into a jus
pepitas, cilantro and epazote with canola oil
faq: Are grits different from polenta?

If you have made polenta, you've made grits: there is no real difference unless you mean lye-processed hominy grits, which are much less common. Arguments about coarser or finer, white or yellow are mainly a distinction without a definitive difference.
How do you cook grits?

Whisk the cornmeal in a thin stream into lots of boiling water (or water and milk), then simmer until smooth, soft and creamy, about 45 minutes here, stirring occasionally and adding water if they dry out. You'll notice a distinct change from gritty to creamy; you can add cheese to enrich.
What are moritas?
Smoked, dried red jalapenos: basically chipotles, but not packed in adobo, so you get all the pepper flavor and smoke without the tomatoey flavors of the canned sauce.
How do you make the leek jus?

Fry the leeks until deep brown and reserve two tablespoons for the dish, then deglaze the pan with 1 cup of water, add toasted morita peppers and honey, simmer five minutes, strain pressing well, and adjust to a thin jus with a hint of body.
Is the epazote pesto overpowering?
The author expected it might be, but it was present and appetizing, not over the top.
What is the idea behind the dish?
Breakfast for dinner that goes beyond pancakes or eggs and toast, mixing sweet, savory and salty flavors in a Southwestern spin on a Southern idea.

summary: Leftover mujadara and shiitake soup: dried shiitake soaked in boiling water (5 minutes in the microwave plus 10-15 minutes resting) into a strong broth, simmered with the sliced mushrooms and 2 cups of leftover mujadara and garnished with parsley and olive oil; serves 2.
glance: 2 cups mujadara (rice, lentils and caramelized onions)
2 good handfuls of dried shiitake, soaked and strained
faq: What do I do with leftover mujadara?
Make it a soup: combine it with shiitake broth and sliced shiitake and bring to a simmer. The savory flavors of the mushrooms and caramelized onions make a rich base for the lentils and rice.
How do I make shiitake broth quickly?

If you have dried shiitake in the pantry you can have a rich stock in 15 or 20 minutes: cover the mushrooms with water, microwave about 5 minutes until boiling (or do it on the stove), rest 10-15 minutes, then strain through a fine mesh strainer, squeezing the juice out of the mushrooms.
What else can shiitake broth do?
The author uses it a lot as the vegetarian base for stir-fry sauces instead of chicken broth.
Is it vegan?
Yes, it's vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free, provided your mujadara was (it's vegan if made with oil instead of butter).
How do I garnish it?
With parsley, a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil, sea salt and fresh ground pepper.

summary: Baby zucchini and blossoms with a cheater sofrito: onion, garlic and chili flakes browned about 5 minutes, tomato paste cooked to a rust-colored paste, loosened with red wine, then whole baby zucchini cooked partly covered about 10 minutes and finished with parsley and squash blossom petals; serves 4 as a side.
glance: 1/2 pound baby zucchini, halved only if over 1/2 inch across
about 10 minutes partly covered, after about 10 minutes for the sofrito
faq: How do I avoid being overrun with zucchini?
Pick them when they are tiny and delicious. A dozen woody, pithy, flavorless giant zucchini is an unpleasant chore, but this recipe happily uses a dozen baby ones along with most of the blossoms.
What is cheater sofrito?

A sofrito that uses tomato paste instead of whole tomatoes to reduce the cooking time: cook onion, garlic, chili flakes and salt until the onion starts to brown, then add tomato paste and continue until it is a rust-colored paste.
How do I cook the baby zucchini?

Stir in the red wine to loosen the sauce, add the zucchini, partially cover the pot and cook, stirring occasionally, until fully tender, about 10 minutes. Add parsley and the blossom petals at the end.
What should I do with leftovers?
Fill a bowl with pinto beans, top with the zucchini and sauce, microwave, and top with smoked cheddar, a fried egg, cilantro and hot sauce.
What if I have more zucchini blossoms?
The author links to another blossom recipe for any extras.

summary: Chermoula, a North African herb sauce: cilantro, parsley, garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, ginger, chili, saffron, coriander, olive oil, lemon juice and salt buzzed in a mini food processor into a rough sauce in about 5 minutes; yields about 3/4 cup.
glance: mini food processor, spice grinder or mortar and pestle, to a moderately rough texture
tastes better made an hour or so ahead
faq: What is chermoula?

A North African sauce typically used as a marinade for fish in its home territory, though it can also be used as a stuffing or sauce. The author served it on a harissa-spiked tagine of butternut squash, potatoes and chickpeas over couscous.
How do I make chermoula?

Combine all the ingredients in a mini food processor, spice grinder or mortar and pestle and process until a thick, moderately rough sauce forms, still a little rough, not fully pureed. It's five minutes of work.
Can I change the recipe?

Yes. There are many variations: some use only cilantro and others add parsley, some use preserved lemon and others fresh juice. This version uses smoked paprika and a bit of fresh ginger. Adapt it to your mood and what's on hand.
Should I make it ahead?
It tastes even better if you make it an hour or so in advance to let the flavors develop.
Is a mortar and pestle better?
The traditional route; the standard claim is that the result is incomparably better than anything made with a motor, which the author says might even be true.

summary: Spaghetti with lobster mushroom: a pound of diced lobster mushroom sauteed with garlic and thyme, either in butter for about 10 minutes for a soft, sweet flavor or fried hard in oil for a browned one, tossed with spaghetti, lemon juice and asiago or parmigiano; serves 4.
glance: 1 pound lobster mushroom, cleaned and cut in 1/2-inch dice
butter, about 10 minutes until tender and sweet; or oil in two batches to brown and caramelize
Vegetarian; vegan if you omit the cheese and use oil instead of butter
faq: What is a lobster mushroom?

Not really a mushroom (nor a lobster): a parasitic fungus that grows on a host mushroom, turning it red and rendering the original mushroom unidentifiable. This enormous one weighed just over a pound.
Does it taste like lobster?

The author's test piece, fried thin and well browned, was distinctly gamey, so he didn't play on the lobster idea. He'd like to try a big mushroom "steak" with huckleberry chutney that plays off the forest gaminess.
Should I brown the mushroom or not?

The author tried both. In a crowded pan it didn't brown and instead developed a softer, sweeter flavor (butter option); frying in two batches over high heat without stirring much browns and caramelizes it (oil option).
Can I use other mushrooms?
Yes, you could do something similar with other varieties of wild mushroom, or even a mixture.
How do I finish the pasta?

Boil the spaghetti to al dente, drain and toss with a bit of butter or olive oil, add lemon juice to the mushrooms, and top the pasta with the mushrooms and cheese. Add the thyme toward the end of cooking.

summary: Aloo tikki, Indian street-food potato fritters: boiled, cooled and mashed potatoes mixed with peas, breadcrumbs, turmeric, ginger and toasted ground coriander and cumin, formed into 2 1/2-inch patties and fried about 2 minutes per side; makes 10 in 20 minutes active (40 total).
glance: 1 pound russet or Yukon Gold (about 4 medium)
about 2 minutes per side in 1/8 inch of oil
faq: What is aloo tikki?

One of the classic street foods of India: simple mashed potato fritters sold by vendors on street corners in Delhi, each with a special technique and loyal customers. They are crispy on the outside and creamy on the inside, two bites each.
How do I keep the fritters from falling apart?
Cool the boiled potatoes thoroughly before peeling and lightly mashing (a potato ricer is ideal), then press the patties fairly firmly, 2 1/2 inches across and 3/4 inch thick, with moistened hands.
How do I cook them?
Fry in about 1/8 inch of oil over a medium-high flame until golden brown, about 2 minutes on each side, drain on paper towels and finish with flaky sea salt.
What spices do I toast?
Coriander and cumin seeds, over a medium-low flame about 1 minute until fragrant but not burned, then ground in a mortar and pestle or spice grinder.
What do I serve with aloo tikki?
The author suggests banana raita for an incredible combination of tastes.

summary: A quick potluck chickpea salad with feta: two cans of chickpeas, red onion, cucumber, roasted peppers, 8 ounces of crumbled feta, garlic, basil, lemon juice and olive oil tossed together, where the feta dissolves into a creamy dressing; serves 12 as a side.
glance: serve right away, or refrigerate a few hours
faq: Why is it a good potluck recipe?

It takes about five minutes from pantry staples like canned chickpeas, roasted peppers and good olive oil, and still has big flavors. The author made it after getting home at 5:30 for a 6:00 block party, and it was gone quickly.
How does the dressing form?
As you toss it, the crumbled feta dissolves a little bit and makes a creamy dressing.
Do I need to add salt?
Taste first and add salt as needed. Depending on how salty your feta is, you might not need any.
How long can it be made ahead?
Serve right away, or it can be refrigerated for a few hours.
What can I add or substitute?
Other herbs (tarragon or dill), olives, green beans, artichoke hearts or just about any vegetable.

summary: Caramelized pear "cupcakes" with blue cheese frosting: puff pastry layered with skillet-caramelized pear rounds and smoked paprika in mini muffin tins, baked 15-17 minutes at 350°F and piped with a blue cheese and cream cheese icing; makes 6, a first-try sweet-savory appetizer.
glance: about 1/3 Pena Azul blue cheese to 2/3 cream cheese with lemon juice, no salt
pretty good for a first try; the author would try Gorgonzola dolce and phyllo
faq: What is the idea behind this recipe?
Sweet savories and savory sweets. The author asked what would go with blue cheese frosting, and his wife said pears. It was his first try at a totally new area of cooking.
How do I make the pear cupcakes?

Cut the caramelized pear slices and puff pastry into circles with cutters, layer pastry, pear and a pinch of smoked paprika in buttered mini-muffin tins, finish with a layer of pastry and bake about 15-17 minutes at 350°F.
How do I make the icing?

Warm the blue cheese and cream cheese about 30 seconds in the microwave until beatable, whisk in lemon juice until smooth, and don't add salt, since you want to garnish with salt. Pipe on with a pastry bag or a snipped ziplock.
What would the author change?
He thinks the Pena Azul was too salty and would try Gorgonzola dolce, would try phyllo instead of puff pastry, and would use mini parchment cupcake wrappers and pipe the frosting more carefully.
How do I serve them?
As an appetizer with a good sherry.

summary: Grilled eggplant and tofu otsu noodles: soba with a tahini, tamari, rice vinegar, lemon and ginger dressing, tossed with cucumber, grilled eggplant and browned tofu, served cool or at room temperature on iceberg lettuce; serves 4 and travels well to potlucks.
glance: 9 ounces soba, boiled about 4 minutes and rinsed in cool water
1/4 cup toasted sesame paste (tahini), tamari, rice vinegar, lemon zest and juice, ginger, Sriracha
faq: What are otsu noodles?
The author realized that by "sesame noodles" people mostly mean a dish made with peanut butter and wheat-based noodles, while what he makes (sesame paste dressing, soba) is much closer to otsu.
Is it good for a potluck?
Yes, it's served cool or at room temperature, and it's a vegetarian dish that easily pleases meat eaters who like Asian flavors.
How should the dressing taste?
Fairly liquid, not pasty, and highly flavored. Taste and adjust: more salt, acid, heat, or thinning. Let it sit for the flavors to develop while you make the noodles and vegetables.
Can I change the vegetables or sauce?
The author thinks the dish likes umami flavors more than green vegetation (shiitake rather than zucchini). Good sauce variations include miso, wasabi and/or fresh garlic.
How do I prepare the eggplant and tofu?

Brush eggplant rounds with oil and grill or broil until deep brown and thoroughly tender, then cut into batons. Pat tofu dry and saute in a single layer over high heat until browned on all sides, or use a pre-flavored tofu.
